newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sees 5 pct precision engineering growth.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees 5 pct precision engineering growth.

text.p: Output from Singapore's precision engineering sector is expected to grow about five percent in 1997, the Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Monday.

"We should see the PE (precision engineering) sector growing by at least five percent in 1997," Gerald Goh, head of EDB's mnaufacturing systems industry development division, told reporters at a briefing.

He said the 1997 growth would be on the back of an expected recovery in Singapore's electronics industry in the second half of 1997. A significant portion of precision engineering's output is geared towards supporting the electronics industry.

Output from precision engineering in 1996 was expected at Singapore $10 billion (US$7.1 billion), a marginal increase of 2.2 percent over 1995, EDB said. This is the lowest growth in the last five years, said Goh.
Fixed investment commitments reached S$663 million, rising 5.4 percent from 1995.
The three largest contributors to output were engineering plastic components, machine tool and industrial machinery, and precision toolings.
Machine tool and industrial machinery generated an output of S$1.1 billion in 1996, up 9.7 percent from 1995.
Engineering plastics components had an output of S$1.6 billion in 1996. Precision toolings produced output of S$611 million.
Output from semiconductor equipment was S$359 million, rising 26 percent from 1995. Output from leadframes, a key component for assembling integrated circuit chips, fell 2.2 percent to S$324 million.
Connector output reached S$434 million, while the optics sector contributed S$135 million.
